description: §6.5.1 a method call on a NESTED reactive path (`@o.list.push(t)`) that is not the first statement of its block still runs. #add runs `const t = 1` then `@o.list.push(t)`; #refill runs `@o.m = [9]` then `@o.m.push(1)`. Carried on impl#1 (S432, P7): the second statement is dropped from the output.
rationale: §6.5.1: a mutating method called on a reactive cell performs that method's ordinary JavaScript mutation and notifies the cell's subscribers. Nothing in §6.5.1 or in the statement grammar makes a statement's effect depend on its position in the block, so both push calls run: after #add then #refill, @o is { list: [1], m: [9, 1] } and the two length readouts show 1 and 2.
